newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks open lower, trade near unchanged.
newsitem.headline: French stocks open lower, trade near unchanged.

text.p: French shares opened slightly lower but immediately moved into positive territory in a market which lacked a firm impetus for an overall direction, dealers said.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 0.24 points or 0.01 percent at 2,229.05 at 0916 GMT.
Dealers said activity was relatively calm overall in volume of slightly over one billion francs at about 0930 GMT. By mid-morning the market failed to break out either upward or downward.

Eurotunnel was off 3.21 percent at the open after an overnight fire in the tunnel injured 34 people and forced the tunnel to close. Authorities said they expected to have the tunnel operating in some capacity by midday.

Eurodisney was off 3.06 percent at 11.20 francs, down from its opening price, after company reported results earlier on Tuesday. The company reported profits of 202 million francs for the 1995/1996 year, at the top end of expectations.
But Eurodisney's chairman said next year would be tough.

"Persistent weakness in the economy, constant pressure on our prices and the strong increaes in financial charges constitute several real challenges for the future, particularly in 1997," Philippe Bourguignon said in a statement.

Shares in French insurer GAN fell 7.23 percent to a new year low at 109 francs shortly after the start of trading as investors reacted to uncertainty over the outcome of a battle between the company's chairman and the government.
"There are tensions between the company and its chief shareholder, the state, and that's never good for a company," one trader said.
Shares in CIC were a tiny bit higher, up 0.31 percent at 322 francs.
On Monday the finance ministry called for the resignation of GAN chairman Jean-Jacques Bonnaud because he refused to support a government plan to privatise the company's banking unit CIC.
On Tuesday morning, Bonnaud said he would not resign, but a government source said he will be removed by decree next week.
"There will be a decree ending his mandate," said the source. The name of a replacement was likely to be decided the same day, the source added.
Axime and Sligos were the biggest gainers of the morning, up 3.23 percent and 3.35 percent respectively, in afterglow of agreed merger and due to arbitrage plays on the stocks.
Axa was up 1.41 percent at 301.2 francs after French regulators approved its merger with UAP, which was up 1.12 percent.
Eiffage leading loser so far, 5.85 percent at 180.30 francs. Dealers said word in the market is the company is having problems.
Canal Plus off 0.48 percent at 1,233 francs after a French court dismissed a court case by broadcaster TF1 against the pay-TV station. TF1 shares rise 0.37 percent at 537 francs.
